questions.stem: In the medallion architecture, which layer holds raw data as it arrived from the source?
questions.explanation: Bronze keeps the raw ingested data, silver holds cleaned and conformed data, and gold holds business-level aggregates and models.

questions.stem: Quarry Lane's store files arrive every few minutes, and only new files should be processed each run. Which ingestion pattern fits?

options.text: A full reload of every file each run
Copying the bucket to a laptop
Incremental ingestion that tracks which files were already loaded

questions.explanation: Auto Loader, for example, keeps the metadata of discovered files in its checkpoint, so each file is processed exactly once and each run handles just the new arrivals.

questions.stem: What is the difference between batch and streaming ingestion?

options.text: Batch only reads CSV; streaming only reads JSON
Batch processes a bounded set of data per run; streaming processes data continuously as it arrives

questions.explanation: Batch reads a bounded set at a time; streaming treats the source as unbounded and processes new data as it arrives, continuously or in triggered runs.

questions.stem: Where should cleaned, deduplicated and type-corrected data live in the medallion architecture?
questions.explanation: Silver tables hold validated, cleaned and conformed data built from bronze.

questions.stem: Put the medallion layers in the order data flows through them.
questions.explanation: Data lands raw in bronze, is cleaned in silver, and is aggregated or modeled for consumption in gold.
